prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Desktop Companion", "Select a friend to join you on your screen daily.", "Select Pet Character"]
1: ["Your Pet is Ready for Your Desktop!", "Your pet is active in your taskbar. Right-click or press shortcut keys to interact anytime."]
2: ["Save Your Companion", "Sign in now to lock in your pet choice and sync across devices."]
3: ["Bringing Your Pet to Life", "We are generating custom animations and setting up desktop behavior.", "Preparing asset models..."]
4: ["Returning user? Sign in with your original account method to keep your existing pet."]
5: ["How Would You Like to Start?", "Pick a ready-to-play companion or craft your own unique pet."]
6: []
7: ["Meet Your New Desktop Buddy!", "Click finish to launch your companion directly onto your screen. You can drag them anywhere!", "Summon Pet to Desktop"]
8: ["We will send a system notification when your pet is ready to spawn!"]
9: ["Official Adoption Certificate"]

verdicts.problem: Creates urgency by telling users to sign in now to lock in their pet choice
